subject: Security

findings.subject: Security
findings.title: No authentication is registered anywhere in the app; a destructive endpoint is fully anonymous

evidence.excerpt:
public static void ApiWebApplicationBuilder(this WebApplicationBuilder builder)
... builder.Services.AddVersioning(); ... AddEndpointsApiExplorer(); ... AddControllers(...)  // no AddAuthentication()/AddAuthorization()

findings.recommendation: Register an authentication scheme (e.g. JWT bearer or the org's identity provider) via services.AddAuthentication(...), call app.UseAuthentication()/UseAuthorization() in the request pipeline, and remove [AllowAnonymous] from TestingController (or restrict it to an authenticated/internal-only policy) so the state-changing /reset action cannot be invoked by an unauthenticated caller.

findings.subject: Security
findings.title: No function-level access control distinguishes sensitive actions from public ones

evidence.excerpt:
public static void ApiWebApplication(this WebApplication webApp)
{ ... webApp.OpenApiWebApplication(); webApp.LoggingWebApplication(); webApp.SwaggerWebApplication(); webApp.UseMiddleware<UnhandledExceptionMiddleware>(); webApp.MapControllers(); }

findings.recommendation: Add services.AddAuthorization() and app.UseAuthorization() to the pipeline, define policies/roles, and apply [Authorize] with the appropriate policy to state-changing actions (e.g. TestingController.ResetTesting) so every sensitive action is checked server-side rather than uniformly allowing anonymous access across both controllers.

findings.subject: Security
findings.title: Zero Trust violation: every reviewed endpoint implicitly trusts any network caller

evidence.excerpt: public static void ApiWebApplication(this WebApplication webApp) { ... no UseAuthentication()/UseAuthorization() call ... }

[HttpGet]
[Route("about")]
...
public IActionResult About(
	[FromQuery(Name = "show-details"), BindRequired] bool showDetails = false)

findings.standard: OWASP Zero Trust Architecture Cheat Sheet
findings.recommendation: Apply explicit verification per-request instead of implicit network trust: require an authenticated/authorized caller identity for every endpoint, and gate the showDetails=true branch of /about (which discloses full application configuration) behind an authenticated, least-privilege policy rather than exposing it to any anonymous caller.

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: No AddAuthentication/UseAuthentication is registered anywhere in Program.cs or ApiExtensions.cs, and the state-changing TestingController.ResetTesting endpoint carries [AllowAnonymous].

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: No AddAuthorization/UseAuthorization or [Authorize] policy exists; SystemController and TestingController both carry blanket [AllowAnonymous] with no function-level distinction between low- and high-sensitivity actions.

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: No JWT issuance or validation code exists in the files in scope; the reviewed controllers and extensions use no bearer-token authentication.

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: No OAuth2 client or server flow code (authorization code, redirect URI, state parameter) is present in the files in scope.

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: No session or cookie-based authentication is used; the API is stateless and every reviewed endpoint is [AllowAnonymous] with no session state.

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: No password or credential storage code exists in the files in scope (TestingController only resets test data rows, not credentials).

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: No custom cryptography or credential hashing code exists in the files in scope.

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: No pipeline-level authentication/authorization exists, and the /about endpoint can disclose full application configuration to any anonymous caller via showDetails=true.

notes: Scope was the two listed controllers, ApiExtensions.cs and Program.cs. To confirm whether authentication/authorization is configured at all, also read the closely-related src/PilotUtiltyApi.Web/Extensions/ApplicationInjectionExtensions.cs and src/PilotUtiltyApi.Services/Extensions/ServicesInjectionExtensions.cs (both call chains invoked from Program.cs); neither registers AddAuthentication/AddAuthorization. No JWT, OAuth2, session/cookie, or password-storage code was found in scope, so SEC-IA-03/04/05/06/07 are N/A. If authentication is intentionally delegated to an external gateway/reverse proxy not present in this repo, that mitigates SEC-IA-01/02/08 but was not evidenced in the files reviewed.
